market_holds: Spot $0.7413 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-19 18:09 UTC): -42% over 20 sessions, -8.8% over 5, -87% from the 52-week high, 2% above the low, and -67% since the close after Q2 ($2.28, 2026-08-14), with no company 6-K since 2026-08-13 (EDGAR submissions API). Market cap about $26m on 35.6m shares, net debt about $117m (stockanalysis.com, 2026-11-19), plus $26.5m of Odds Holdings deferred consideration due by 2027-04-01. Up to 70% of that can be paid in shares, which at spot would be about 36m new shares, roughly doubling the count. No usable option chain and no EDGAR reaction history, so the bar comes from bars and from 20-day realised vol of 87% (about 5.5% a day). Last two reactions: Q1 (2026-05-14, FY guide cut to $165-170m revenue and $45-50m adj. EBITDA, 25% layoffs) opened -31% and closed -42%; Q2 (2026-08-13, guide reaffirmed) opened +13% and closed +19%. Consensus is stale: FY26 revenue $165.4m (the bottom of the guide), last revised 2026-08-14, so about 97 days old. Q3 revenue estimates run $41.5-42.1m and EPS $0.04-0.09. Average target $4.43 on 8 analysts against a $0.74 price, so the price plainly does not believe consensus or the guide. Short interest is 5.6% of float with 6.1 days to cover, which is not crowded. The run-in has two tied parts: the 2026-10-16 Catena Media profit warning (GRSD $1.35 to $1.10 by 10-30), and a -17.5% day on 4x volume on 2026-11-04 that I could not tie to any news.
view: The print turns on whether management keeps the FY26 guide, and on what it says about paying for the $26.5m deferred consideration. The guide needs H2 adj. EBITDA of $28.3-33.3m against H1's $16.7m and Q2's $7.7m, and H2 revenue of $86.8-91.8m against H1's $78.2m. Only about $6.5m of that comes mechanically from the May restructuring. The rest needs marketing revenue to recover and data to grow more than 50%. The best counterparty evidence since the company last spoke points against the marketing half. Catena Media's Q3 North American revenue fell 29%, after roughly +21% in H1, and Catena said operators were tying affiliate spend to sportsbook budgets and cutting it. DraftKings said its core marketing excluding Predictions fell year on year in Q3, while its Predictions spend was mostly local. Prediction-market spend is a real offset that GRSD named in Q2, when North American marketing grew 63%, but it is not enough to make a reaffirmation the likely case. So I expect a trim or cut to the FY guide, or a reaffirmation that leans hard on Q4, more often than a clean hold. The cost savings should still show as a visible sequential margin step from 20%. Against that, the price already discounts a lot. The equity is a $26m stub on roughly $165m of claims, it has lost two-thirds since a reassuring quarter without a word from the company, and it has already absorbed the Catena read-through. A cut to around $40-45m of EBITDA with a cash plan for the deferred consideration could be read as a relief. A cut with an equity settlement, a covenant amendment or going-concern language would take the stub lower. The probabilities lean down, but the two outcomes are close in size and both are large, so the edge is too thin to recommend.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the H2 marketing shortfall: consensus revenue, last touched in August, still sits at the bottom of the guide although counterparties showed affiliate budgets cut in Q3. But the price ($0.74, about 3x EV/EBITDA on the guide) already sits far below that consensus, so I cannot show that the price, as opposed to the stale estimates, holds the guide. The gap I can show is in the estimates, not clearly in the price.

recommendation.reason: The mechanism for a lower guide is dated and public: Catena's Q3 North American collapse and operators' affiliate cuts against an H2 EBITDA ramp of 70-100%. But the price has fallen 67% since the last reaffirmation and 45% since the Catena warning, so most of a cut may already be in a $26m stub. A cash plan for the deferred consideration could turn a cut into a relief rally. A 58% lean does not reach the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A reaffirmed $45-50m EBITDA guide with Q3 adj. EBITDA of $12m or more and a stated cash or credit-facility route for the April 2027 deferred consideration (no share settlement) would make the stub rally hard, as Q2's reaffirmation opened +13%.

self_critique: The stock has already fallen two-thirds on no company news, so the market may be pricing something worse than a modest guide trim. Management reaffirmed in August despite SEO declines and has a growing data business (OpticOdds, Perplexity). The restructuring savings make a sequential margin jump close to guaranteed, and prediction-market operators spent heavily into the NFL season and use affiliates. A guide trimmed only to the low end, plus a cash plan for the deferred consideration, could give a +20-40% squeeze on a $26m float-light stub, as Q2's reaffirmation gave +13% at the open. That case is strong enough to keep me near the middle rather than at 35.
